title: Ponugoti Twins Build Robotics Nonprofit That Has Reached More Than 1,200 Students
excerpt: Vivaan and Virat Ponugoti started Blast Robotics in Berwyn, Pennsylvania, after one of them was turned away from his school team. Eighteen months on, their Keystone STEM Alliance has mobilized more than $215,000 in support — and runs workshops as far away as Telangana.
body:
• Twin brothers Vivaan and Virat Ponugoti, students at Conestoga High School in Berwyn, Pennsylvania, founded FIRST Robotics Competition Team 10989, Blast Robotics, on June 4, 2025, and incorporated the nonprofit Keystone STEM Alliance on August 4, 2025.
  • In 18 months the initiative has mobilized more than $215,000 in cash and in-kind support, engaged over 100 students and reached more than 1,200 young people, according to New India Abroad.
  • The project began with a rejection: Virat reached the VEX World Robotics Competition in Dallas in 2024, while Vivaan was not admitted to the same school program because of limited capacity.
  • Through its STEM2Ignite outreach, the Berwyn nonprofit has also run robotics sessions in India, including a December 2025 workshop for 165 girls in Kodakandla, Telangana. Families can reach the team at hello@keystonestemai.org.

Two Indian-American twin brothers in Pennsylvania have turned a school robotics rejection into a nonprofit that, in a year and a half, has mobilized more than $215,000 in cash and in-kind support and reached more than 1,200 young people. Vivaan and Virat Ponugoti, students at Conestoga High School in Berwyn, founded Blast Robotics — FIRST Robotics Competition Team 10989 — and the Keystone STEM Alliance, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit built to give students barrier-free access to robotics education.

The setback that started it

The brothers' own account, published by the Keystone STEM Alliance, traces the project to 2024. Virat earned a spot in his school's VEX Robotics program and helped lead his team to the VEX World Robotics Competition in Dallas, Texas. Vivaan, despite experience with Arduino, Raspberry Pi, programming and game development — and a showing at the Chester County Invention Convention — was not admitted to the same program, which had limited capacity and a selective screening process.

Instead of dropping the interest, Vivaan attended FIRST Robotics Competition events as a spectator with his mother and came away with a plan: build the open-door version of the program himself, in the Main Line area outside Philadelphia. In the summer of 2025 the brothers volunteered at a robotics camp at Lower Merion High School, then borrowed VEX kits and ran their own camp in Berwyn for 13 students in grades 5 to 9, in workspace offered by EADEH Enterprises.

From a team to a nonprofit

Blast Robotics was created on June 4, 2025. Two months later, on August 4, 2025, the brothers partnered with Hari Ponugoti to incorporate Keystone STEM Alliance Inc., giving the work a nonprofit structure for fundraising, mentorship and programs beyond a single competition team. The alliance now runs the robotics team, a summer camp and Scouting America Venturing Crew 181 from Berwyn.

The scale since then is what drew coverage from New India Abroad and Philadelphia's 6abc: more than $215,000 in cash and in-kind support mobilized in 18 months, over 100 students engaged and more than 1,200 young people reached, with a team of about 40 members. In its rookie season in 2026, Blast Robotics earned the Rookie All-Star and Rising All-Star awards, according to the alliance's timeline.

An ocean away: the Telangana connection

The brothers' second program reaches back to India. During a 2024 visit, Virat and Vivaan met students and teachers in rural schools and began planning STEM2Ignite, an outreach initiative designed to bring mobile STEM labs and hands-on robotics to underserved communities. Through that program, Blast Robotics students have led robotics awareness sessions in Telangana, including at the Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institutions and the TS Residential School for Girls; in December 2025, the team's co-captains led a workshop for 165 girls at the Telangana Residential School and Junior College for Girls in Kodakandla. The alliance describes the details on its global outreach page.

What families can do

Keystone STEM Alliance is based at 15 Waterloo Ave, Suite 200, in Berwyn, Pennsylvania, and runs programs for students in the Philadelphia region, including its summer camp for grades 5 to 9. Families interested in the team or its camps can contact the alliance at hello@keystonestemai.org or through its website. For diaspora parents, the Ponugoti story carries a practical lesson the brothers state plainly in their own history: the door that closed — one selective school program — became the reason a much larger door now exists for other people's children, on two continents.
